text: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house will stand firm as the highest of the mountains, lifted above the hills, and the peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths." For instruction goes out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for strong nations far and wide. They will hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation, nor will they train for war anymore.
Everyone will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make him afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.

versions.text: Everyone will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
versions.explanation: Number/pronoun mismatch: the verse begins with the singular "Everyone ... his own" but shifts to plural "them." Keeping the singular "him" preserves internal agreement and reads smoothly aloud.

text: Though all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
On that day, declares the LORD, I will gather the lame and bring together the scattered, those I have afflicted.
I will make the lame a remnant and the exiled a mighty nation, and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
And you, watchtower of the flock, stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come—the former dominion will return, the kingship of the daughter of Jerusalem.
Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor perished, that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and groan, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you must leave the city and camp in the open field. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued, there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you, saying, "Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand his plan, that he has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples. You will devote their unjust gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now marshal your troops, daughter of troops! A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.

versions.text: Now marshal your troops, city of troops! A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads bat-gedud, "daughter of troops," matching the "daughter of Zion" imagery used elsewhere in the chapter (vv. 8, 10, 13). "City of troops" loses that verbal link. A footnote could note the alternative sense of the verb: "Or 'gash yourself'."
